Since \(S_7>S_8\), we have \(a_8=S_8-S_7<0\).  
Since \(S_8>S_6\), we have \(a_7+a_8=S_8-S_6>0\).  
Thus \(a_7>0\) and \(a_8<0\), so \(d=a_8-a_7<0\).

Let \(a_n=a+(n-1)d\). From \(a_7>0\) and \(a_8<0\),
\[
a+6d>0,\qquad a+7d<0.
\]
Dividing by \(d<0\) gives
\[
-7<\frac ad<-6.
\]
Also \(a_7+a_8>0\) gives
\[
2a+13d>0 \implies \frac ad<-\frac{13}{2}.
\]
So
\[
-\frac{13}{2}>\frac ad>-7.
\]
Let \(t=-\frac ad\), then \(\frac{13}{2}<t<7\).

The nonzero root of
\[
S_n=\frac n2(2a+(n-1)d)
\]
is
\[
n=1-\frac{2a}{d}=1+2t.
\]
Since \(\frac{13}{2}<t<7\),
\[
14<1+2t<15.
\]
Thus \(S_n>0\) for \(n\le 14\) and \(S_n<0\) for \(n\ge 15\). Therefore
\[
S_{14}S_{15}<0.
\]

\boxed{14}
